title: Local generator of $\mathcal O_C(D)$; $\mathcal O_C(D)$ is invertible
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field and $C$ a smooth connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], with generic point $\eta$ and function field $k(C)=\mathcal O_{C,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field]; by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings] $C$ is integral, $\mathcal O_C(V)\subseteq k(C)$ for every nonempty open $V$, and for every closed point $Q$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{C,Q}\subseteq k(C)$ is a discrete valuation ring with normalized valuation $v_Q$. Let $D=\sum_Qn_Q[Q]\in\operatorname{Div}(C)$ be a divisor [def-sc-divisor] and $\mathcal O_C(D)$ the sub-$\mathcal O_C$-module of the constant sheaf $k(C)$ of [def-sc-divisor]: for a nonempty open $V\subseteq C$,
$$
\mathcal O_C(D)(V)=\{g\in k(C):\ g=0\ \text{or}\ v_Q(g)+n_Q\ge0\ \text{for every closed point }Q\in V\},
$$
and $\mathcal O_C(D)(\emptyset)=0$. Let $P$ be a closed point of $C$ and $t\in\mathcal O_{C,P}$ a uniformizer. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $P$ such that
$$
\mathcal O_C(D)(V)=t^{-n_P}\cdot\mathcal O_C(V)\subseteq k(C)\qquad\text{for every nonempty open }V\subseteq U .
$$
Consequently: $\mathcal O_C(D)$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] (on $U$ the map $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_C(D)|_U$, $a\mapsto t^{-n_P}a$, is an isomorphism); its stalk at $P$ is $\mathcal O_C(D)_P=t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}\subseteq k(C)$; and $\mathcal O_C(0)=\mathcal O_C$ as subsheaves of $k(C)$.

proof.text:
*Choice of $U$.* Since $t$ is a uniformizer of the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_{C,P}\subseteq k(C)$ [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings, clause 3], $t
eq0$ in the field $k(C)$ and $v_P(t)=1$. Let $S_1$ be the set of closed points $Q
eq P$ with $n_Q
eq0$; it is finite because $D$ is a finite formal sum [def-sc-divisor]. Let $S_2$ be the set of closed points $Q
e P$ with $v_Q(t)
eq0$. $C$ is a Noetherian integral scheme [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings, clause 1], so it has a finite affine open cover with Noetherian coordinate rings; every closed point $Q$ has $\mathcal O_{C,Q}$ a discrete valuation ring, hence of dimension one, so $Q$ has codimension one, and there $\operatorname{ord}_Q(a)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{C,Q}/a\mathcal O_{C,Q})=v_Q(a)$ for $0
e a\in\mathcal O_{C,Q}$ (the chain $\mathcal O_{C,Q}\supset\pi\mathcal O_{C,Q}\supset\dots\supset\pi^{m}\mathcal O_{C,Q}=a\mathcal O_{C,Q}$, $\pi$ a uniformizer, has $m=v_Q(a)$ successive quotients isomorphic to the residue field), so $\operatorname{ord}_Q=v_Q$ on $k(C)^*$; by the finiteness of zeros and poles [lem-sc-divisor-finite-support] applied to $t$, $S_2$ is finite. Put $S=S_1\cup S_2$, a finite set of closed points not containing $P$; a finite union of closed points is closed, so $U:=C\setminus S$ is an open neighbourhood of $P$. By construction, for every closed point $Q\in U$: if $Q
eq P$ then $n_Q=0$ and $v_Q(t)=0$; and $v_P(t)=1$.

proof.text: *Sections of $\mathcal O_C$ inside $k(C)$.* Identify $\mathcal O_C(V)$, for nonempty open $V$, and $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ with their images in $k(C)$ under the injective germ maps [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings, clause 1]. Claim: for every nonempty open $V\subseteq C$, $\mathcal O_C(V)=\{g\in k(C): g\in\mathcal O_{C,Q}\text{ for every closed point }Q\in V\}$. If $s\in\mathcal O_C(V)$ and $Q\in V$, then $s_\eta$ is the image of the germ $s_Q\in\mathcal O_{C,Q}$, so $\subseteq$ holds. Conversely let $g$ lie in $\mathcal O_{C,Q}$ for every closed $Q\in V$. Every point of $V$ is either a closed point or $\eta$ [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings, clause 2], and $\mathcal O_{C,\eta}=k(C)$ contains $g$; so $g$ lies in the image of $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ for every $x\in V$, and by [lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue] (applied to the integral scheme $C$ and the nonempty open $V$) $g$ is the image of a section of $\mathcal O_C(V)$.

source.place: Algebra Lemma 031T (algebra-lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1), part (2), $R=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=1}R_{\mathfrak p}$, as used in Divisors Lemma 0BE8 (divisors-lemma-normal-c1-injective), last sentence; on a curve the height-one primes are the closed points and the sheaf form is lem-sc-function-field-sections-glue

proof.text: *Comparison of $\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$ with $t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_C(V)$.* Let $V\subseteq U$ be a nonempty open and $g\in k(C)$. If $g=0$ then $g\in\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$ and $g=t^{-n_P}\cdot0\in t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_C(V)$. Let $g\neq0$ and $Q\in V$ a closed point. By step 1, if $Q\neq P$ then $v_Q(t^{n_P}g)=n_Pv_Q(t)+v_Q(g)=v_Q(g)=v_Q(g)+n_Q$; if $Q=P$ then $v_P(t^{n_P}g)=n_P+v_P(g)$. So in all cases $v_Q(t^{n_P}g)=v_Q(g)+n_Q$. For a discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_{C,Q}$ with fraction field $k(C)$ and valuation $v_Q$, a nonzero $h\in k(C)$ lies in $\mathcal O_{C,Q}$ iff $v_Q(h)\ge0$ [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings, clause 3]. Hence, by the formula for $\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$ [def-sc-divisor], $g\in\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$ iff $t^{n_P}g\in\mathcal O_{C,Q}$ for every closed $Q\in V$, iff $t^{n_P}g\in\mathcal O_C(V)$ by step 2, iff $g\in t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_C(V)$. This proves $\mathcal O_C(D)(V)=t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_C(V)$ for every nonempty open $V\subseteq U$.

source.place: Divisors Lemma 0BE9 (divisors-lemma-local-rings-UFD-c1-bijective), proof, first paragraph: the canonical section of $\mathcal O_X(D)$ vanishes exactly along $D$; here: $t^{-n_P}$ generates $\mathcal O_C(D)$ on $U$

proof.text: *Invertibility.* For a nonempty open $V\subseteq U$ let $\phi_V:\mathcal O_C(V)\to\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$, $a\mapsto t^{-n_P}a$ (products in $k(C)$), and $\phi_\emptyset=0$. By step 3 $\phi_V$ is well defined and surjective; it is injective since $t^{-n_P}\neq0$ in the field $k(C)$; it is $\mathcal O_C(V)$-linear since the module structure of $\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$ is multiplication in $k(C)$ [def-sc-divisor]; and it commutes with restriction, because for $V'\subseteq V$ both restriction maps are inclusions of subsets of $k(C)$ (for $\mathcal O_C$ the germ at $\eta$ of $s|_{V'}$ equals that of $s$). So $\phi:\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_C(D)|_U$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. Every closed point $P$ has such a neighbourhood $U$, and the generic point $\eta$ lies in any of them (a nonempty open contains $\eta$, and $C$ has a closed point by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings, clause 2]); since every point of $C$ is closed or $\eta$, these opens cover $C$. Hence $\mathcal O_C(D)$ is locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_C$, so it is quasi-coherent and locally free of rank one, i.e. an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Divisors Lemma 0BE9 (divisors-lemma-local-rings-UFD-c1-bijective), proof, first paragraph: $\mathcal O_X(D)$ is invertible as the sheaf of an effective Cartier divisor (Lemma 0AGA); here written out for a curve

proof.text: *Stalk at $P$.* The open neighbourhoods $V\subseteq U$ of $P$ are cofinal among all open neighbourhoods of $P$, so the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is $\mathcal O_C(D)_P=\varinjlim_{P\in V\subseteq U}\mathcal O_C(D)(V)$, a filtered colimit of subgroups of $k(C)$ along inclusions, hence equal to their union inside $k(C)$. By step 3 it is $t^{-n_P}\bigcup_{P\in V\subseteq U}\mathcal O_C(V)$, and $\bigcup_{P\in V\subseteq U}\mathcal O_C(V)=\mathcal O_{C,P}$ inside $k(C)$ (the same colimit for $\mathcal O_C$, whose germ maps to $k(C)$ are injective [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings, clause 1]). So $\mathcal O_C(D)_P=t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}$.

source.place: Divisors Lemma 0AGA (divisors-lemma-weil-divisor-is-cartier-UFD), proof: the stalk of the ideal of $D$ at $x$ is $(f)\subset\mathcal O_{X,x}$; here the inverse $t^{-n_P}\mathcal O_{C,P}$

proof.text: *$\mathcal O_C(0)=\mathcal O_C$.* For $D=0$ and nonempty open $V$, the formula of [def-sc-divisor] gives $\mathcal O_C(0)(V)=\{g: g=0\text{ or }v_Q(g)\ge0\ \forall\text{ closed }Q\in V\}=\{g:g\in\mathcal O_{C,Q}\ \forall\text{ closed }Q\in V\}$ (DVR, [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings, clause 3]), which is $\mathcal O_C(V)$ by step 2; both sheaves are $0$ on $\emptyset$, and the restriction maps of both are inclusions in $k(C)$.

lean.statement: theorem Divisor.module_local (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (C : Scheme.{u}) (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve f] [Smooth f] (D : C.Divisor) : letI : IsNoetherian C := isNoetherian_of_locallyOfFiniteType f letI : IsRegular C := IsRegular.of_smooth f letI : IsIntegral C := (C.smooth_connected_curve_local_rings k f).choose let M := D.moduleOfSmoothConnectedCurve k C f ∀ (P : closedPoints C) (t : C.presheaf.stalk P.val), IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (C.presheaf.stalk P.val) = Ideal.span {t} → let c := (algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk P.val) C.functionField t) ^ (-D P) (∃ U : C.Opens, P.val ∈ U ∧ ∀ (V : C.Opens), V ≤ U → Nonempty V → ∃ e : Γ(C, V) ≃ₗ[Γ(C, V)] D.sectionModule C V, ∀ (a : Γ(C, V)) (x : V), (e a).val x = c * algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk x.val) C.functionField (C.presheaf.germ V x.val x.property a)) ∧ M.IsInvertible ∧ (∃ j : M.presheaf.stalk P.val →ₗ[C.presheaf.stalk P.val] C.functionField, Function.Injective j ∧ (∀ (V : C.Opens) (hP : P.val ∈ V) (s : D.sectionModule C V), j (M.presheaf.germ V P.val hP s) = s.val ⟨P.val, hP⟩) ∧ Set.range j = {g : C.functionField | ∃ a : C.presheaf.stalk P.val, g = c * algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk P.val) C.functionField a}) ∧ (∀ V : C.Opens, ((0 : C.Divisor).sectionModule C V : Set (V → C.functionField)) = Set.range (divisorScalarMap C V))
